由于江苏泗阳匪患盛行，我离开泗阳前往魏营（镇江埠），打算在这个地区购买小麦，然后运往上海出售。由于从事这种生意无利可图，我停止了购买小麦，但留在魏阳，在那里我遇到了我的朋友张亚经（Chang Ya Ching）和李大模（Lee Ta Moh）。这两人和我提议在魏阳建立一家名为“福兴行”的染坊，总资本为20,000.00元，这笔钱分为二十股，每股1,000.00元。张亚经同意投资2000.00元（2股），李大模投资3,000.00元（3股）。梁智明和纪清凯各给了我1,000.00元，我也将这些钱投入了拟建的染坊，

带着这7,000.00元，加上我自己的5,000.00元（总计 - 12,000.00元），我来到上海。途中在宝应（Pau-ying）遇到了一位老朋友，名叫罗大兆（Loh Ta Chao），他当时请求我带上他的

LOH TS TSING ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ), 48, Married,
Tungchow, -- C.P.C.No. 172,

My name is Loh Ts Tsing, and I am the proprietor and business
manager of the Yah Sing Navigation Co. Room No. 1, 2nd.Floor,
Route No.25, Rue de Consulat.

One day, during the latter part of November, 1938,
my friend Chang Ts Vai approached me, requesting my assistance
to purchase a consignment of cigarettes, which he and his friend
Ts Yoong Tsiu, would ship to inland cities for sale. I was
asked to purchase the cigarettes at the end of January, 1939,
when he would detail his friend Ts Yoong Tsiu to attend to the
matter.

On the 20th. January, 1939, Ts Yoong Tsiu came to my
house, producing a note of introduction written by Chang Ts Vai,
and informed me that the time had arrived for the purchase of
the consignment. Shortly afterwards, I succeeded in purchasing
on their behalf, 6 cases of "Pirate" and 6 cases of "Champagne"
Cigarettes, which were entrusted to the Yah Hsing Koong Shipping
Agency, Siking Road, for transportation to Zai Yang Kong, Foo
Nying Hsien. Two "Delivery Orders" were issued by the above
agency to Ts Yoong Tsiu, who soon travelled to Zai Yang Kong
waiting for the arrival of the cargoes. During that period
Chang was away from Shanghai.

About a month afterwards, Chang Ts Vai, came back to
Shanghai and complained that the consignment of cigarettes had
not arrived at its destination all these days. Therefore, on
the afternoon of 23.2.39 I accompanied Chang to the Yah Hsing
Koong Shipping Agency lodging a severe complaint to that effect.
Mr. Zau Pah Hsuin of the shipping agency informed us that the

我叫陆志晋，是协新轮船公司的业主和业务
经理，办公地点位于领事馆路25号二楼1室。

1938年11月下旬的一天，
我的朋友张树藩找到我，请求我协助
购买一批香烟，他和他的朋友
赵永秋 (Ts Yoong Tsiu) [音译] 将把这批香烟运往内地城市销售。我被
要求在1939年1月底购买这批香烟，
届时他将指派他的朋友赵永秋处理此事。

1939年1月20日，赵永秋来到我家，
出示了张树藩写的介绍信，并通知我购买这批货物的时间已到。不久之后，我成功代表他们购买了6箱“海盗牌”和6箱“香槟牌”
香烟，并将其委托给西京路亚兴公 (Yah Hsing Koong) 轮船代理行，运往阜宁县戴场港 (Zai Yang Kong, Foo Nying Hsien)。上述代理行向赵永秋签发了两张“提货单”，他随即前往戴场港等待货物到达。在此期间，
张树藩不在上海。

大约一个月后，张树藩回到上海，并抱怨这批香烟至今未到达目的地。因此，在1939年2月23日下午，我陪同张树藩前往亚兴公轮船代理行，就此提出严厉投诉。代理行的邹柏勋 (Zau Pah Hsuin) [音译] 先生告诉我们，

装载我们要运送的香烟的“海达”号 (Hai Tah) 轮船，

    鉴于这种情况，我们写信给我们在阜宁的人员，要求他们将两张提货单通过邮件寄回上海。然而，在这两张提货单到达之前，我们成功从邹先生那里获得了两份副本，凭此我们可以随时从浦东的仓库中提取货物。

person (s).

The members of the Gendarmerie adhered to these
conditions, and the raid was carried out without any
untoward incident.

From enquiries made, and perusal of translation of
the seized documents it is apparent that neither of the
arrested men are guerillas, their purpose in coming to
Shanghai, being to purchase dye stuffs and machinery with
which to establish a "Dying Works" at Hwei-ying Hsien,
Northern Kiangsu. This however, will be investigated,
whilst the Gendarmerie for their part have promised to
produce the three persons who implicated the arrested
man. The full details covering the arrest, and investigations
made are contained in a diary submitted by D.S.I, Konovaloff.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

N. L. Glover

Umemoto of the S.P.Office, requested assistance from the S.M.P. on behalf of the Japanese Military Police Headquarters, Bridge House, to effect the arrest of a male Chinese, named CHANG TS VAI (張樹基), who was alleged to be the battalion commander of a mobile unit, setting the time for raid at 6 a.m. on the following morning : 12.3.39.

Accordingly, at the appointed time, Sgt. Major Katoda and three other members of the Japanese Military Police, accompanied by J.D.S. Sugemoto and J.D.C. Yamahara of the S.P. Office, came to C.1. H.Q.C.B. for the necessary assistance.

On being requested to produce an informer or some documentary evidence against the wanted man, Chang Ts Vai, Sgt. Major Katoda stated that the Japanese Military Police had on the 4.3.39, arrested three male Chinese in the Western District, O.O.L. whom, he stated, were members of a mobile unit. Upon interrogation, one of them named Yang (楊) implicated in his statement the wanted man as being the battalion commander of the mobile unit who had come to Shanghai for the object of purchasing firearms for the mobile units operating in Foo-Nying Area.

Sgt.Major Katoda further emphasized that according to the information which he had obtained, Chang Ts Vai had already purchased some firearms and sent them to the Foo-nying Area, North Kiangsu. He further stressed that Yang, the man in their custody who had implicated Chang Ts Vai, would identify the latter who could be located at Room 719, Yangtse Hotel, 287 Yunnan Road.

My name is Chang Ts Val, age 35, native of S-yang,
married, and residing at Room No. 719 The Yangtsze Hotel,
Yunnan Road.

I was born in See Ka Ko Za, Nan-Shiang, S-yang Hsien,
Kiangsu (江苏). I have parents, brother, sister
and wife in my native place, making a total of nine members
in the family. I own 800 mow of land and 14 houses in the above

taking with me my family, evacuated to Bang-Boo, where, after
staying for several months, I left for Kying Yang Kwen,
Anhwei, because the city of Bang-Boo also fell into the
hands of Japanese.

From Kying Yang Kwan I evacuated to Sen Ho Chinen,

then Canton and Hongkong, whence I came to Shanghai by

以下为张士伟（Chang Ts Val，原文如此，前文作张树藩）的供词，籍贯泗阳 ____ ，由我（警员编号172）于1939年3月12日在中央捕房总部刑讯室 ____ 录取，并由S. F. Hau翻译/口译。

我叫张士伟，35岁，泗阳籍，已婚，现居住于云南路扬子饭店719号房间。

我出生于江苏泗阳县南乡四家阁子（See Ka Ko Za, Nan-Shiang）。我在家乡有父母、兄弟、姐妹和妻子，全家共九口人。我在上述地方拥有800亩土地和14栋房屋。幼年时我就读于泗阳高等小学，18岁时转入泗阳中学。两年后完成学业。随后我开始协助父亲务农。同时，我谋得永和（Wing Wo）杂货店经理一职，我是该店的股东之一。

30岁时（1934年4月），经我的朋友、苏州警察局局长徐志?（Syee Chi S）推荐，我加入苏州警察局，担任副督察。我一直担任此职，直到当前战事爆发，苏州被日军占领后，我失业了。我带着家人撤离到蚌埠（Bang-Boo），在那里停留数月后，因蚌埠也落入日军手中，我前往安徽泾阳关（Kying Yang Kwen）。

means of a steamer.

On arrival at Shanghai, I went to engage Room No. 219
the Mung Yue (孟月) Lodging House, Hupeh Road, where
I stayed for 4 days. I then returned to my native place,
S-Yang. Three months later I was still unemployed and
the place where I was living was frequently visited by
bandits; I, therefore, suggested establishing the "Dyeing
Works Factory" using the name "Fo Shing Han" in Kwei-ying (桂陽)
Hsien. After collecting a sum of $12,000.00 as capital,
I, carrying with me this sum of money, came to Shanghai
and arrived on 2.2.39.

I first made my abode at Room 134 The Yah Chiu (亞九)
Lodging House. Four days later, at the instigation of
one named Sung S Sz (宋士), accountant, of the Yangtsze
Dacing Hall, I removed from this lodging house to Room 719
The Yangtsze Hotel, and it was then when I deposited the
money which I was carrying with me at the Kiangsu Farmers
Bank. I was going to purchase some dye stuffs in Shanghai
when I learned in the newspaper that Kwei-ying and S-y:ng
had been captured by the Japanese army. On learning this
information I kept this matter in abeyance until such
time when the situation of the above two cities became
normal.

During the period of my stay in the Yangtsze Hotel,
I became acquainted, through the introduction of Sung
S Sz, with a girl named Chen Su Tsung, a professional
dancer. This girl often called on me at my room.

One day, another dancer, named Soo San informed me that
a paramour of Chen Su Tsung (陳素珍) had accused me of
being a sweet-heart of the latter. I however, told Soo San
(蘇三) that it was merely a rumour.

In Jan. 1939 in S-yang, I together with a friend, named
Tsu Yoong Chiu (朱永秋), prepared a sum of money and

我从泾阳关撤离到皖豫边界的沈丘县（Sen Ho Chinen），随后前往河南安川县（'an-Chuen hsien，原文不清，可能为安阳或类似地名），接着是荥阳（Shing yang），然后是汉口，再是广州和香港，由此乘轮船来到上海。

抵达上海后，我去湖北路孟月（Mung Yue）旅馆租了219号房间，在那里住了4天。随后我返回家乡泗阳。三个月后，我仍然失业，且居住地经常有匪徒出没；因此，我建议以“发新恒”（Fo Shing Han）的名义在桂阳（Kwei-ying）县创办“染织厂”。筹集了12,000.00元作为资本后，我携带这笔款项来到上海，于1939年2月2日抵达。

我最初住在亚九（Yah Chiu）旅馆134号房间。四天后，在扬子大戏院会计宋士（Sung S Sz）的怂恿下，我从该旅馆搬至扬子饭店719号房间，也就是在那时，我将随身携带的钱款存入江苏农民银行。我本打算在上海购买一些染料，但从报纸上得知桂阳和泗阳已被日军占领。得知这一消息后，我将此事搁置，直到上述两城局势恢复正常。

在扬子饭店逗留期间，通过宋士的介绍，我结识了一位名叫陈素珍（Chen Su Tsung）的职业舞女。这名女子经常到我的房间来访。

有一天，另一位名叫苏三（Soo San）的舞女告诉我，陈素珍（陳素珍）的一个情夫指控我是她的恋人。但我告诉苏三（蘇三），那仅仅是谣言。

1939年1月在泗阳，我和一位名叫朱永秋（Tsu Yoong Chiu）的朋友准备了一笔钱，

intended to do some business together. With this money
Tsu bought some "Kao-liang" wine in our native place and
transported it to Shanghai where it was re-sold and then
bought 10 boxes of "Pirate" cigarettes which we intended
to take and sell in Foo Nying, Kompo. This consignment
was then entrusted to the Yah Shing (杨兴) Transportation
Co. to be conveyed to Foo Nying, Kompo (date unknown).
The cargo was shipped to Foo Nying on board S.S.
"Hai-Tuh", which was unfortunately stopped and detained
by a Japanese war ship before its arrival in Foo Nying.
Tsu Yoong Chiu was therefore, unable to get the
cargo in Foo Nying. At that time I was already in
Shanghai. Tsu later sent by post the delivery order of
the 10 cases of cigarettes to Mr. Wong Wei Foo (王惠孚)
of the China Native Products Company, Nanking Road. Wong
in turn gave the delivery order to me. With this order
I went to interview Mr. Zau of the Yah Shing Transportation
Co., Siking Road. Zau (赵) informed me that the cigarettes
were already in Shanghai and were being stored in the ware-
house in Pootung. He further promised me that as soon as
he received the cigarettes he would sell them for us.
The above is my true statement.

Signed:Chang Ts Vai.

"Hai-Tuh"）运往高邮，不幸的是，在抵达高邮之前被一艘日本军舰拦截并扣留。因此，朱永秋无法在高邮提取货物。当时我已在上海。后来朱通过邮局将10箱香烟的提货单寄给南京路中国国货公司的王惠孚（Wong Wei Foo）先生。王随即将提货单交给我。凭此单据，我去西康路杨兴运输公司拜访赵先生（Mr. Zau）。赵（赵）告诉我，香烟已经到达上海，正存放在浦东的仓库里。他还向我承诺，一旦收到香烟，就会替我们出售。以上是我的真实供词。

签名：张树藩（Chang Ts Vai）。

The following is the statement of Loh Ts Siang ( 陸子祥 )
native of Yang-wo, Sue-chi, Kiangsu taken by me C.D.C. 2
at C.I., C.B.H.Q. on the 12.3.39 translated and interpreted by Clerk Hsia

My name is Loh Ts Siang, age 26, native of Yang-wo( 洋沃 ),
Sue-chi ( 宿遷 ), Kiangsu, married, merchant, residing at
Room 719 Yangtsze Hotel, No.281 Yunnan Road.
I graduated from the Yang Wo Primary School ( 洋沃小學 ),
and afterward Sue-chi Junior Middle School ( 宿遷初級中學 )
in boyhood. Later, my parents passed away and I was in finan-
cial difficulties. At that time I assisted my fifth uncle and
second brother working in a grocery entitled "Loh Yih Tai"
( 陸益泰 ) in my native place.
During the month of November, 1937, was spread to our
native place, my uncle, brother and myself evacuated to Pau-
ying ( 寶應 ). During the spring, 1938, I felt sore all over
my body and an ulcer appeared in the region of waist. There
was no good doctor to attend me to cure my sickness. On the
14th. February, 1939, my brother's friend named Chang Ts Vai
( 張樹藩 ) came to Shanghai for business, therefore my
brother asked me to accompany him to Shanghai to attend a
doctor. On the same day, we, Chang and myself, started at
Pau Ying by steamer, through Taichow ( 泰州 ), Taishing ( 泰興 ),
Sing-kong ( 新港 ) and Wu-yoh ( 武穴 ). We arrived at Shanghai
on the 23.2.39, we then proceeded to the Native Products
Emporium ( 國貨商場 ), Nanking Road, visiting one named Wong
Wei Fu ( 王惠孚 ), one of my class-mates, and explained why
I had come to Shanghai. Later, Chang Ts Vai accompanied me to
the Dah Kung Hospital ( 大公醫院 ) on Gordon Road for treatment.
I was detained there about one week, but Chang visited me
frequently. One day, Chang visited me again and told me that

本人姓名陆子祥，年龄 26 岁，籍贯江苏宿迁洋沃（Yang-wo），已婚，商人，现寓云南路 281 号扬子饭店 719 室。
本人幼年毕业于洋沃小学，后就读于宿迁初级中学。其后父母双亡，本人陷入经济困境。当时本人在家乡协助五叔及二哥经营一家名为“陆益泰”的杂货店。
1937 年 11 月间，战事蔓延至本人家乡，本人随叔父及兄长撤离至宝应（Pau-ying）。1938 年春季，本人感到全身疼痛，腰部出现溃疡。因无良医诊治，病情未愈。1939 年 2 月 14 日，本人兄长之友人张树藩（Chang Ts Vai）来沪经商，故兄长嘱本人陪同其来沪就医。当日，本人与张树藩乘轮船自宝应出发，途经泰州（Taichow）、泰兴（Taishing）、新港（Sing-kong）及武穴（Wu-yoh）。我们于 1939 年 2 月 23 日抵达上海，随后前往南京路国货商场，拜访本人同学王惠孚（Wong Wei Fu），并向其说明来沪缘由。之后，张树藩陪同本人前往戈登路大公医院接受治疗。本人在该院留治约一周，期间张树藩频繁探视。一日，张树藩再次探视并告知本人，

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Removal of two slot machines from
No.68 Broadway by Japanese.

Acting on instructions from D.D.O."C", Sen. Detec.
i/c Hongkew, instructed me to approach the Japanese
Consular Police to ascertain the intention of the
**〔此处转录不清〕** authorities as to the eventual disposal of
the two slot machines removed by them from No.68
Broadway.

In accordance with the above instructions, at 1.35 p.m.
this day, I proceeded to the Consulate Building, P.A. to
see Mr. Hashizume of the Japanese Consular Police Section,
when he intimated to me that the slot machines in question
would be returned to owner against the owner's written
apology in which she should admit her wrong in dis-
regarding the repeated warnings given prior to the
eventual removal of the machines by the Consular Police
and to promise not to operate the machines in future.

The above Mr. Hashizume further intimated to me that
this action of removing slot machines had been taken
by the Consular Police in accordance with the Japanese
Naval Law.

日本人从百老汇路 68 号移除两台老虎机。

遵照“C”区副总监（D.D.O."C"）之指令，虹口高级探长指示本人接触日本领事馆警察，以查明 **〔此处转录不清〕** 当局对于由其从百老汇路 68 号移除的两台老虎机最终处置之意旨。

根据上述指令，本人于当日下午 1 时 35 分前往领事馆大楼，拜访日本领事馆警察科的桥爪（Hashizume）先生。他向本人表示，涉案老虎机将归还给业主，条件是业主须提交书面道歉信，承认其在领事馆警察最终移除机器之前无视多次警告的错误，并承诺今后不再运营这些机器。

上述桥爪先生进一步向本人表示，移除老虎机之举是领事馆警察依据日本海军法律采取的行動。
